From “where?” to a shortlist in three moves

  1. Say who is moving

    Pick one of 27 profiles or answer a few questions to build your own. The weights stay visible, so you always know why a place ranks.

  2. Choose where to look

    A whole country, a region or a single canton or département. Narrow it by size, airport, big-city or sea distance.

  3. Compare and decide

    Every place gets a scorecard, trends, close alternatives and local context. Save favourites, compare side by side and print a booklet for the visit.

Questions people ask

How does Nestlyzer decide where I should live?

You pick who is moving, for example a young family or a retired couple. Each profile weights categories such as costs, safety, family, jobs, mobility and environment. Nestlyzer scores every municipality in the country you choose and ranks them. Every weight and source is listed on the methodology page.

Which countries are covered?

45 countries: 35 in Europe, plus the United States, Canada, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, Hong Kong, Singapore, Australia, New Zealand and Israel, with 128,466 places in all. Switzerland has the deepest data (28 official factors including municipal tax burden). Austria adds age structure. The other European countries use population, density and growth plus geographic measures such as airport and big-city distance; outside Europe the places, their population and local names come from GeoNames, with the same geographic measures.

Is it free and do I need an account?

It is free and there is no account. Your shortlist and custom profile stay in your browser.

Can I build my own profile?

Yes. Answer a few short questions about household, budget, daily anchor, mobility, tax sensitivity, climate, language and target countries, then fine-tune the weights. Nestlyzer shows which standard profiles are closest to yours.

Is this financial, tax or legal advice?

No. Nestlyzer is a decision aid built on public statistics. Check taxes, permits, schools, healthcare and housing with the responsible authority or a qualified adviser.

Where does the data come from?

Eurostat GISCO LAU, the Swiss Federal Statistical Office, the Swiss Federal Tax Administration, Statistics Austria, EDJNet population-weighted centres, OurAirports and Natural Earth. Photos and descriptions come from Wikimedia projects and never affect scores.

Legal notice

Operator: Torsten Sauter, Alte Landstrasse 77, 8706 Meilen, Switzerland. Contact: torsten.sauter@icloud.com.

Nestlyzer is a research and decision-support website. It is not a public authority, financial adviser, tax adviser, real-estate broker, medical adviser, immigration adviser or legal adviser. Imprint and policies

Privacy

There is no account system and no server-side user profile. Searches, filters, saved places and guided-profile answers stay in your browser. Public enrichment calls go to official data services, Wikimedia, Wikidata, OpenStreetMap and map tile servers, which receive normal technical request data. Visit statistics (Google Analytics) and the ad service load only after you agree.

User relocation preferences are never sold or used for advertising.

Minimum disclosure

Scores are decision aids. Verify taxes, residence rules, school access, healthcare, housing, noise, transport, permits and property details with the responsible authority or a qualified adviser. Country-specific tax outputs are only reliable where that country's tax module is joined.

Photos, coats of arms, public text, contact links, advertising and cross-border notes do not affect the score.

Sources and licences

Public datasets and media keep their own terms. OSM-derived data requires attribution. Creative Commons and Wikimedia media may require creator, source and licence attribution. Boundaries are for visualisation and are not cadastral documents.
